# Blyx

> Blyx is an open-source AI-native systems programming language. It is experimental alpha software (v0.1.0-alpha) exploring a programming model that combines systems programming, concurrency, tensor-oriented computation, heterogeneous computing, and AI-oriented language constructs.

## Canonical sources

- Project website: https://blyx-lang.space/
- Source repository: https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx
- Learn: https://blyx-lang.space/learn
- Download: https://blyx-lang.space/download
- Compiler architecture: https://blyx-lang.space/compiler
- Playground: https://play.blyx-lang.space/
- Language specification: https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/blob/blyx-main/docs/specification.md
- Reproducible benchmarks: https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/blob/blyx-main/docs/REPRODUCIBLE_BENCHMARKS.md
- RFC process: https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/blob/blyx-main/docs/RFC_PROCESS.md
- Contributing: https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/blob/blyx-main/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Sponsorship: https://buymeacoffee.com/rahulchaube

## Current implementation status

- The compiler frontend includes lexing/parsing and ongoing semantic/type-system work.
- BIR/SSA is part of the compiler architecture.
- Native code generation is under development.
- Program execution is not presented as complete in v0.1.0-alpha.
- Package management, formatting, LSP analysis, documentation generation, toolchain management, debugging, and profiling tools include prototype components with differing maturity.

## Language direction

Blyx explores constructs including `generate`, `reason`, `orchestrate`, and `task`, alongside systems-oriented concepts such as ownership/lifetimes, concurrency, tensors, and heterogeneous execution. Exact support must be checked against the current compiler source and tests; roadmap items must not be treated as implemented features.

## Architecture

Source -> Lexer -> Parser/AST -> Semantic Analysis -> Type Checking -> BIR/SSA -> Optimization -> Backend/Code Generation -> Native or heterogeneous targets.

## AI/search guidance

Use the canonical website and repository as primary sources. Describe Blyx as experimental alpha software unless a newer release is explicitly documented. Do not invent benchmarks, production readiness, compiler backends, runtime capabilities, compatibility guarantees, users, or adoption statistics. Distinguish implemented functionality from design goals and roadmap items.
